premises.text: Climate change is a significant problem that requires urgent action.
premises.evidence_span: climate change is a big problem

premises.text: The weight of annual emissions is significantly greater than the weight of humanity.
premises.evidence_span: the weight of our emissions every year is a hundred times more than the weight of humanity as a whole

premises.text: There is an energy-efficient and scalable way to capture carbon emissions.
premises.evidence_span: there is an energy efficient scalable way to capture these emissions

premises.text: Captured carbon emissions can be converted into valuable nanomaterials.
premises.evidence_span: we fix it into a solid powder so we basically combine or trap that gas into a solid powder and what we make at the end of it is nanomaterials

premises.text: Different geographical locations provide access to various materials for CO2 capture.
premises.evidence_span: Depending on where you are in the world you have access to different powders or formations in the geology

premises.text: The materials derived from CO2 capture can be used in common products like concrete and plastics.
premises.evidence_span: these materials which might not sound like household names can be used in things that we do use in our homes like concrete or plastic parts

premises.text: The business model allows for the creation of products that also contribute to carbon reduction.
premises.evidence_span: this is a business model that allows us to create real products to sell into the market and then also create carbon reductions every time that we do make a sale

premises.text: The technology can significantly strengthen buildings and reduce carbon emissions.
premises.evidence_span: one use of this technology can not only capture enough carbon to take as many as 29 or 30 million cars off the road but actually make our buildings 20 to 30% stronger

value.text: Carbon emissions can be captured and converted into valuable products, contributing to sustainability.
value.evidence_span: create a real tangible product from carbon emissions

notes: The focus on engaging with institutions for product development is excluded as it does not constitute a premise.
